summary: Load-balancer sticky-session rotation causes truncated streamed conclusion for chunked SSE sessions
description: Issue summary: BrightDocs reports that long-running server-sent events (SSE) streams sometimes terminate with the final paragraph missing when their clients are routed through our edge LB. The stream arrives and carries most content, but the concluding sentence(s) are not delivered; client receives a clean connection close with no explicit end marker from the app. This is affecting multiple users at BrightDocs and correlates with periods of load-balancer stickiness cookie rotation and backend connection handoffs.
impact: Customer-facing search assistant returns partial answers ~4-8% of streamed sessions during peak traffic windows in us-west. BrightDocs flagged this as material for their SLAs and we have an open enterprise support contract. Multiple downstream users report truncated paragraphs, causing content integrity issues in the product UI.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use BrightDocs test harness with client configured for SSE streaming and chunked transfer-encoding.
2) Send prompts that produce ~800-1200 token responses (long enough to span several SSE events).
3) Simultaneously trigger a simulated edge LB cookie rotation (rotate stickiness cookie or cause conn affinity change) while stream is active.
4) Observe client-side SSE message sequence and final lines; repeat until truncation reproduces (~1 in 25 runs under our repro setup).
observed_behavior:
- Most chunks arrive and client displays content progressively; near the end of the response, the last sentence (a short concluding paragraph) is missing.
- Connection is closed from the server side without a distinct 'end' event.
- No 5xx returned to client; HTTP 200/204 observed depending on path.
- Edge proxy logs show backend session tear-down within 200ms of last received chunk.
- No explicit application error emitted by serving-runtime logs.
expected_behavior: SSE stream should deliver the full content including concluding sentence(s). Any load-balancer/edge affinity change should either allow the stream to complete (graceful handoff) or trigger a reconnect/resume flow that preserves final payload semantics.
logs:
Sample edge-proxy snippet (us-west):
[2026-03-10T14:21:03.432Z] conn=abcd1234 backend=10.2.4.55:8080 read=chunk(1024)
[2026-03-10T14:21:03.887Z] conn=abcd1234 stickiness_rotated cookie=stky_v2 -> stky_v3
[2026-03-10T14:21:04.051Z] conn=abcd1234 backend_close reason=idle_timeout downstream_close=200ms
Serving runtime excerpt:
[2026-03-10T14:21:03.998Z] request_id=bd-req-77 writing chunk N (final content arriving)
[2026-03-10T14:21:04.049Z] request_id=bd-req-77 flush_to_socket=OK
[2026-03-10T14:21:04.050Z] request_id=bd-req-77 socket_eof_detected - downstream RST
Note: client reported no JSON end marker in SSE meta for this request.
investigation_notes:
Hypotheses considered: 1) Edge LB cookie rotation is triggering an affinity reassignment that closes active backend socket before application has finished sending the final chunk; 2) Chunked transfer encoding trailing zero-length chunk or final CRLF is being consumed/stripped by intermediary (LB or CDN) on affinity swap; 3) Serving runtime sends final bytes but upstream socket close races with TCP FIN, leading to last-write loss.
What we tried: - Reproduced with our internal harness by forcing LB stickiness swap; reproduced at ~4% rate. - Captured tcpdump between edge proxy and backend: final FIN appears within 5-25ms of last data packet; last data packet sometimes missing final CRLF when observed by proxy. - Enabled socket linger on backend in a staging cluster; reproduction rate dropped but did not vanish. - Reviewed edge-proxy code path (linked PR) for chunk coalescing and observed a path where trailing zero-length chunk handling is bypassed if connection is flagged for immediate handoff.
Preliminary finding: Race between affinity rotation handler and chunked-stream finalization in edge-proxy; in some code paths proxy issues backend-close before it forwards the last tiny flush (CRLF or trailing delimiter) to client, resulting in client-level incomplete content.
workaround:
- For BrightDocs we recommended decreasing load-balancer stickiness rotation frequency and enabling graceful drain window on edge LB for SSE paths.
- On customer side, application-level guard: emit an explicit sentinel SSE event (data: __STREAM_END__) before closing stream to force delivery of concluding content if any chunk is dropped.
- We temporarily increased backend socket linger to 200ms in the affected edge pool which reduced the rate of truncations.
next_steps:
- Edge-proxy team to add a safety flush of final chunk when connection is flagged for affinity handoff; patch in PR #987 is under review.
- Add E2E test that simulates sticky-cookie rotation during SSE and validates final sentinel arrival.
- Post-deploy: monitor truncated-response metric and set alert threshold for >0.5% per-minute in us-west.
- Add customer-friendly guidance to Streaming best-practices doc (confluence page linked).
